findings.title: Unquoted session directory name makes the recommended inspection command injectable
findings.what: The detector interpolates a session directory name directly into a shell command. A valid directory entry containing shell metacharacters such as `;` or command substitution changes the command when the user copy-pastes the recommended fix, rather than merely selecting that session's JSON files.
findings.fix: Do not construct a shell program from the session identifier. Emit a fixed command that passes the directory as a separately shell-quoted argument, using a proven POSIX shell-quoting helper, or provide a non-command UI action.
findings.acceptance: Add a fixture whose sessionId contains spaces, a semicolon, a quote, and command-substitution syntax; parse the emitted snippet as a shell command and verify the identifier remains exactly one inert path argument and cannot start another command.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 80-86 interpolate the complete sessionId without quoting. The directly related baseline parser derives that value from directory entry names and does not constrain it to UUID characters, so this is reproducible rather than hypothetical.

findings.title: Newlines in task subjects escape the comment-only command snippet
findings.what: The command-target fix is intended to contain comments only, but root and blocked-task subjects are inserted verbatim. A subject containing a newline followed by shell text creates an uncommented executable line when the user copy-pastes the snippet.
findings.fix: Normalize all interpolated subjects to a single line and prefix every resulting physical line with `# `, or change the fix target to non-executable informational text.
findings.acceptance: Create root and child subjects containing `\nprintf owned`; verify every physical line in the emitted command snippet begins with `#` and executing the snippet cannot run the injected text.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed rootSubject and every blocked subject flow verbatim into lines 90 and 92. Task subjects are arbitrary parsed strings, and no newline removal or per-line comment prefix is applied.

findings.title: Seven recommendation detectors omit required structured provenance
findings.where: The recommendation object returned by each cited detector
findings.what: Each detector makes measured and inferential claims, but its returned recommendation has no `provenance` object identifying source artifacts/fields, observed values, and the inference connecting them to the action. Human-readable evidence strings alone do not meet the structured reproducibility gate.
findings.fix: Add `claimClass`, `proofTier`, and `provenance` with typed observations naming the exact input artifact and fields, their computed values, and a bounded inference for every emitted recommendation.
findings.acceptance: For a firing fixture from each detector, `validateRecommendationProvenance(rec)` returns an empty error list and assertions verify the cited source fields and values reproduce the displayed counts/rates.
findings.verifyNote: A separate re-read of every returned object confirmed that all seven end after evidence/fix/view fields without structured provenance. The two provenance-bearing detectors in this batch were used only as implementation-pattern support and are not listed in this finding.

findings.title: Concordance gate performs quadratic work over the full task corpus
findings.what: `divergenceAutonomyConcordance` compares every matched pair with nested loops, performing n(n-1)/2 iterations on every detector evaluation. The input is not capped, so large ingests can turn this recommendation gate into a CPU latency hotspot.
findings.fix: Compute Kendall-style concordance in O(n log n) using sorting plus inversion counting with explicit tie handling, or enforce a documented deterministic sample/budget before pairwise comparison.
findings.acceptance: Add a large-corpus benchmark/probe that exercises at least 100,000 matched rows, verifies the same concordance result as the pairwise reference on smaller randomized corpora, and demonstrates O(n log n) scaling within the detector budget.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed `pairs` includes every matched steering row and lines 139-148 have no cap or early termination; the exact iteration count is n(n-1)/2, so the hotspot is deterministic and reproducible.
